## 2026-11-17 — v0.66.0

### Changed

- **The pre-push hook now blocks a push that adds a HIGH or CRITICAL foxguard finding.** Before, every foxguard finding was a warning. The level is `git config security.foxguardBlock` or `SCRIPT_HELPERS_FOXGUARD_BLOCK` (`off`, `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`; default `high`; with both set the stricter applies). Only findings the push introduces block: one already at the remote's base, also when it moved lines, or below the level, is a warning. At any level but `off` a missing foxguard, a failed scan or a changed file it skips refuses the push; a value that is not a level refuses every push. The foxguard config is read from the base the remote already has, not from the pushed commits, so a push cannot disable its own check; a changed config gets a warning. An inline `foxguard: ignore` comment in the pushed code does not hide a new finding either, nor does a hidden path or one foxguard treats as noise (`vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `build/`, a minified `app.min.js`): each changed file is scanned on its own. A changed file foxguard skips is named with its cause and a fix, not advice to install foxguard. To keep the old behaviour: `git config security.foxguardBlock off`. `setup-hooks.sh --status` shows the level (`foxguard_block=` with `--porcelain`). Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fails without the change; its finding cases skip when foxguard is not installed, `FOXGUARD_REQUIRE=1` makes that a failure).
